input.quote: 12.4 During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter, Customer shall not develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory.
input.rationale: No employee non-solicit or no-hire exists (searches for "solicit", "induce", "hire", "employ", "recruit", "poach" return nothing binding Customer), but § 12.4 is a restrictive covenant binding Customer for twenty-four months with unlimited scope and no carve-out for general recruitment, general advertising, or ordinary business activity. It sits at the playbook walk-away boundary on duration and fails the general-solicitation carve-out requirement, and it directly contradicts § 12.3, where Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no non-compete or no-hire commitment. The minimal edit reaching the preferred position (no restrictive covenant on Customer) is deletion of § 12.4; the fallback is a mutual twelve-month non-solicit limited to personnel involved in the Services with general-advertisement and unsolicited-approach carve-outs.

proposal.summary: Delete § 12.4, the 24-month restrictive covenant binding Customer
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have deleted § 12.4 because our playbook does not accept restrictive covenants binding the Customer, and this one restricts all competing activity for twenty-four months with no carve-out for general recruitment or ordinary business activity. It also directly contradicts § 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no non-compete or no-hire commitment. If Vendor needs personnel protection, we can accept a mutual non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the Services for twelve months after their involvement ends, with carve-outs for general advertisements and unsolicited approaches and no no-hire.
